summary: Tested the signed delivery receipt (law offices) and the admin one-tap 'new PIN by text' end to end. Backend: 17/17 pytest passed. Covered: the trigger for a law-office store with a signature (status 'sent'; mer-1 temporarily set to law_office also gave 'sent' to the Resend test inbox); no receipt without a signature; no receipt for non-law stores; 'no_recipient' when every login is disabled; never sent twice. PDF: valid token gives application/pdf with the tracking code, recipient, address, 'Delivered at ... (Eastern)' and the vector signature polylines; another stop's token gives 403; garbage, expired and session tokens give 400; a missing token gives 422. I also captured the real email HTML by patching send_email in a throwaway script: the link in the email downloads the PDF (200, application/pdf). PIN text: no auth gives 401, merchant and driver give 403, unknown driver gives 404. The admin call returns {ok, invite:'sent', pin:null}, the hash changes, the old PIN gets 401, and two resets give different hashes. The manual PUT PIN flow still works. Frontend (390x844): /admin/drivers shows driver-pin-text-{id} on every row (44px tall). Tapping it shows 'SENDING…' and then the toast 'NEW PIN TEXTED TO TEST_UI PIN'. The RESET PIN, then input, then SAVE flow shows 'PIN SET FOR ...' and the new PIN logs in. No deprecated Expo packages in the files touched.

minor.issue: The email link opens straight in the browser. An expired or invalid link shows raw JSON {"detail": ...} instead of a friendly page, so a law office opening a 31-day-old link sees a JSON error.

There is no per-driver cooldown or rate limit. Repeated taps or calls send one Twilio SMS each, which costs money and can spam the driver. Existing driver sessions (JWT) stay valid after the PIN reset, because tokens are not revoked. The manual PUT /pin has the same behaviour already.

issues: 'NEW PIN BY TEXT' resets the PIN right away with no confirm step. A mis-tap locks the driver out of their current PIN (it stops working). Consider a confirm dialog or an undo option, since 'one tap' was the request.

action_items: Optional: serve a friendly HTML error for expired or invalid receipt.pdf links (opened from email in a browser).
Optional: add a short cooldown (e.g. 60s per driver) on POST /api/admin/drivers/{id}/pin/text, and consider a confirm step in the UI.
Optional: invalidate existing driver sessions when the PIN is reset.
critical_code_review_comments: receipts.send_signed_receipt claims the stop atomically ({receipt_email_at: None} → set), so it never sends twice. But if every send fails, the status stays 'failed' and nothing ever retries it.
The receipt link is a 30-day bearer token (sub=stop_id). Anyone holding the link can download the PII and the signature, and the link can't be revoked. This is acceptable by design but worth knowing.
Twilio returns 'sent' even for fictional 555 numbers (the message is queued), so the 'TEXT NOT SENT — NEW PIN IS …' UI branch could not be exercised live.
seed_data_creation: TEST_ law-office/store merchants, TSRC* cloned stops and TEST_ drivers were all deleted. mer-1 was restored exactly (no business_type or signature_required). Demo driver PINs were never touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=<public url> python -m pytest tests/test_signed_receipt_pin_text.py -n0. pytest.ini adds xdist and the env var is not exported by default. Tests mint receipt tokens with core.issue_token(stop_id,'merchant',purpose='receipt'). Twilio reports 'sent' for 555 numbers, so the new PIN can't be read; the tests check that the old PIN fails instead.
